B.
Business Overview
Overview
We
are an early commercialization stage technology company focused on transforming railway safety through advanced AI-integrated sensing
systems. We develop and commercialize proprietary, multi-spectral electro-optic platforms that provide extended-range situational awareness
and real-time hazard detection. Using machine learning algorithms to identify and classify obstacles, our technology enhances safety,
improves operational efficiency and supports continuity across deployments
Since
our founding in April 2016, we have developed proprietary railway detection systems designed to enhance railway safety and operational
efficiency. Based on advanced image processing and deep leaning technologies, these systems provide real-time warnings to train drivers
of obstacles on and around railway tracks including during severe weather and challenging lighting conditions. Our MainLine system incorporates
high-resolution cameras capable of identifying objects at distances of up to 2,000 meters, together with an onboard computer unit that
uses AI and machine learning algorithms to analyze images and alert train drivers of potential risks.
Our
railway detection systems are based on electro-optic technology, including visible-light and thermal cameras, which transmit data to
a ruggedized onboard computing unit designed to operate in harsh operating environments of locomotives. Image-processing and machine
learning algorithms process the data in real time to detect and classify potential hazards on and around the tracks, including people,
animals, vehicles, signs, signals and anomalies (unclassified objects). These capabilities may also support additional use cases, including
data analytics.
The
ongoing electrification and increasing digitalization of railways are key factors driving growth in the transportation market. The rail
industry is progressively moving toward higher levels of train automation, supported by advanced control, signaling, and monitoring systems
that improve train operations, including braking, acceleration, and station stopping. In parallel, operators are seeking to increase
track capacity and operational efficiency, which depend not only on automation but also on modern digital signaling and traffic management
systems.
Autonomous
trains, often referred to as driverless trains, represent one aspect of this automation trend. These trains are designed to operate with
minimal human intervention and are supervised from centralized control centers. Existing onboard obstacle detection systems autonomously
command trains to slow or stop upon detecting hazards. In the systems currently deployed in the industry today, onboard obstacle detection
technologies are capable of automatically commanding the train to slow or stop when hazards are detected. These technologies provide
real-time notification to operational control centers and the necessary onboard attendants or remote operators for immediate intervention
if required.
As
road traffic congestion increases globally, demand for smarter, higher-frequency, and more reliable rail services continues to rise,
further supporting the development and adoption of autonomous and semi-autonomous train technologies. According to a January 2026 report
by Fortune Business Insights, the global autonomous train market was estimated at $14.6 billion in 2025 and is expected to reach $24.26
billion in 2034, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.8% from 2026 to 2034, driven by governments and transit authorities
increasingly viewing autonomous trains as a solution to congestion, labor constraints, and sustainability goals.

capital would cause dilution to our existing shareholders, and may affect the rights of existing shareholders.
